name: Universal City
seo_title: Universal City Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 3 Events, 2 Free
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Universal City, TX: the free tree lighting at City Hall, Nighthawk Winterfest fireworks and Santa at Olympia Hills.
lede: Universal City packs three free December evenings into its calendar: the city's tree lighting at City Hall, Northeast Lakeview College's Nighthawk Winterfest with fireworks, and a Holiday Jingle and Mingle with Santa at Olympia Hills.
celebrates: The City of Universal City starts December with its Tree Lighting at City Hall on Universal City Boulevard, a tradition the city magazine says began with a few hundred people and now draws a big crowd, with food and drinks donated by local businesses. A few days later, Northeast Lakeview College hosts Nighthawk Winterfest on its Kitty Hawk Road campus, with holiday lights, activities and a closing fireworks show paid for by sponsors. Mid month, Olympia Hills holds a Holiday Jingle and Mingle with free pictures with Santa and a hot chocolate bar. Blue Santa, run by the police department and its Citizens Police Academy alumni, helps local families.
lastyear: In 2025 the Universal City Tree Lighting was held on December 1 from 6 to 8 pm at City Hall, as the city announced in a post from its 55th Veterans Day Parade. The Gateway, the city's community magazine, says the tree lighting began 14 years ago, when Mrs. U.C. Christmas, Cheryl Maxwell, created it, and that it has grown from a few hundred people into one of the city's biggest evenings. The city also held its 56th Veterans Day Parade in November 2026.
facts: Universal City sits across the Union Pacific Railroad tracks from the main gate of Randolph Air Force Base, according to the Texas State Historical Association. Randolph Field opened on October 25, 1931, and developer Aubrey Milner named Universal City that same year. The city incorporated in 1960. Olympia Hills opened in March 2000, and Northeast Lakeview College's campus opened in fall 2008 on land shared with Live Oak. The 2020 census counted 19,720 residents.
trains: Universal City grew up beside the Union Pacific Railroad tracks that run past the main gate of Randolph Air Force Base, the Handbook of Texas says. The nearest Amtrak stop is the San Antonio station at 350 Hoefgen Street, served by the Sunset Limited and the Texas Eagle. Families who love trains can visit the San Antonio Railroad Heritage Museum in Elmendorf on Saturdays, ride the Longhorn and Western Railroad at the Texas Transportation Museum in San Antonio, or book the Hill Country Flyer from Cedar Park.
train_links: Railroad memorabilia in the Elmendorf Public Library at 203 Bexar Ave, open Saturdays 9 am to 5 pm.
A San Antonio museum founded in 1964, with rides on its Longhorn and Western Railroad included in admission.
The Hill Country Flyer, a 66-mile round trip from Cedar Park to Burnet, and the North Pole Flyer each December.
traditions: The city lights its tree at City Hall on Universal City Boulevard with food and drinks donated by local businesses and s'mores.
Northeast Lakeview College fills its campus with holiday lights and activities, and the night ends with a fireworks show.
Olympia Hills offers free pictures with Santa and a hot chocolate bar on a December weeknight.
Universal City police and the Citizens Police Academy Alumni run the program, with applications through the city.
The city's winter festival returns each February, a reminder that the season does not end with Christmas.
kidfact: Universal City sits right next to Randolph Air Force Base, which opened as Randolph Field in 1931. The town got its name that very same year.
faq: When is the Universal City tree lighting?

The City of Universal City holds its Tree Lighting at City Hall, 2150 Universal City Boulevard, on an early December evening. It has run in recent years from 6 to 8 pm and is free. The city lists the date on its events calendar and in The Gateway magazine, so check there for this year's details.

Nighthawk Winterfest is a free holiday evening hosted by Northeast Lakeview College at 1201 Kitty Hawk Road in Universal City. The college fills the campus with holiday lights and family activities, local vendors set up, and the night ends with a fireworks show. Sponsors cover the costs so admission stays free.
Where can kids see Santa in Universal City?

Olympia Hills, the city's golf course and conference center at 12900 Mount Olympus, hosts a Holiday Jingle and Mingle in December with free pictures with Santa and a hot chocolate bar. The City of Universal City lists it in The Gateway magazine. Santa and Mrs. U.C. Christmas also come to the free tree lighting at City Hall.
How does Blue Santa work in Universal City?

Blue Santa is run by the Universal City Police Department and the Universal City Citizens Police Academy Alumni. Families apply with a form posted on the city's website, and applications close in early December. The city shares the deadline each year on its website and Facebook page, so check there in early November.
Where is the nearest Amtrak station to Universal City?

The nearest Amtrak station is in San Antonio at 350 Hoefgen Street, served by the Sunset Limited and the Texas Eagle. Closer to home, Universal City sits beside Union Pacific tracks near Randolph Air Force Base. The Texas Transportation Museum in San Antonio offers train rides on its Longhorn and Western Railroad.
highlights: The City of Universal City's free Tree Lighting is Tuesday, December 1, 2026, 6 to 8 pm at City Hall, 2150 Universal City Blvd (city events calendar).
Northeast Lakeview College hosts the free Nighthawk Winterfest on Friday, December 4, 2026, 5:30 to 8 pm at 1201 Kitty Hawk Rd, ending with fireworks (college Winterfest page).
Olympia Hills holds a Holiday Jingle and Mingle on Thursday, December 17, 2026, 5 to 9 pm at 12900 Mount Olympus, with free pictures with Santa and a hot chocolate bar (The Gateway, Oct/Nov 2026).
The Gateway says the tree lighting was created 14 years ago by Mrs. U.C. Christmas, Cheryl Maxwell, and has grown from a few hundred people (City of Universal City magazine).
Universal City sits across the Union Pacific tracks from Randolph AFB's main gate; Randolph Field opened October 25, 1931, the year the town was named (Handbook of Texas).
